about: MUTATING — re-register ONE worker's Longhorn DEFAULT disk whose record no longer matches the disk under it (infra/forge/reregister-longhorn-disk.sh <node> <plan_sha256>) through the forge's ops_kubectl door (the admin kubeconfig David placed, infra/estate/ops-credentials.sh), reading the disk's own longhorn-disk.cfg through the ops_talosctl door. Filed as backlog 36d2c484 on 2026-10-21: w-2's default-disk-080400000000 at /var/lib/longhorn read Ready=False DiskFilesystemChanged ('record diskUUID does not match the one on the disk'), Schedulable=False, storageMaximum 0, on a 929 GiB filesystem with 886 free — the record predates the 1 TB disk that replaced w-2's system disk — so Longhorn could place one 100 GiB worker volume cluster-wide, and no door reached a default disk (add-longhorn-disk and remove-longhorn-disk act only on u-<volume> at /var/mnt/<volume>). AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape, as the longhorn-disk family is: it declares requires_approval with the read-only plan-a-longhorn-disk-reregistration (this script's --plan) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and patches nothing unless today's plan hashes to it. Once applied Longhorn reads the disk Ready, so a second run of the same approval is refused: at most once. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM: a registry node whose role is talos-worker, with the cluster agreeing on its address and carrying no control-plane label (refused before any door opens); a Longhorn node reading Ready=True; exactly one disk at /var/lib/longhorn, named default-disk-<hex> — the packet names a node, never a disk or a path; Longhorn reading that disk Ready=False with reason DiskFilesystemChanged; the disk's longhorn-disk.cfg naming a diskUUID that is not the record's; and a record that holds NOTHING by four readings over both UUIDs (no replica on either diskUUID or on its node and path, no scheduledReplica or scheduledBackingImage in Longhorn's diskStatus, storageScheduled 0, no backing image file on either UUID) — or nothing is done (exit 78). THE WRITE is three kubectl patch --type=json compare-and-sets: (1) TEST spec.disks is exactly the map the plan read and REPLACE the record's allowScheduling with false (skipped when already false); then, after a 15 s settle, the holdings are read AGAIN, and anything now naming the record stops the run (exit 1) with it left unschedulable and nothing removed; (2) TEST spec.disks is the plan's map with the record unschedulable and REMOVE it, then read the node every 10 s for up to 300 s until Longhorn drops its status for the record, where the stale diskUUID lives; (3) TEST spec.disks is the plan's map without the record and ADD it back — the same name, path, storageReserved, tags and diskType, schedulable — so Longhorn reads the file on the disk and records its diskUUID; tried three times, because until it lands the node has no default disk record, and if Longhorn never dropped the stale status the record is added back all the same, leaving the node as it read before, and the run exits 1. Nothing else is written: the files under /var/lib/longhorn and every other disk are untouched. THE EFFECT IS READ BACK: every 10 s for up to 300 s, the Longhorn node; only when spec.disks reads as the plan said it would and Longhorn's own status for the disk reads Ready=True and Schedulable=True with the diskUUID the file on the disk names (no other disk's) and a storageMaximum above zero is the effect line printed, and otherwise the run exits 1 saying the re-registration is NOT proven with Longhorn's own reason. Timeout 1260: the plan's reads again (up to ~300 s with a first image pull), the scheduling patch, the settle and the second read (~100 s), the removal and its 300 s wait, the re-add (three tries of 20 s, 10 s apart), and the script's own 300 s read-back, which gives its verdict before the runner's kill.
effect: ^reregister-longhorn-disk: [a-z0-9-]+ has Longhorn disk default-disk-[0-9a-f]+ at /var/lib/longhorn re-registered — read back: Ready=True, Schedulable=True, diskUUID [0-9a-f-]+ \(the one on the disk\), storageMaximum [0-9]+ bytes, and its [0-9]+ other disk\(s\) unchanged \(after [0-9]+s\)$
